chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Why Edgar Sampson left the band
summary: Sampson quit after a fight at a Maryland dance because he would not travel South.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Is that eventually why Sampson left the big band?

No. He left the band because he didn't want to go on the road. We played Virginia -- down in Maryland some place. And it was a big fight. It was the first fight we ever had. Some guy came there and wanted to break up the dance, or something. He was throwing bottles and everything, and Sampson left and came back home. He didn't want to go South with us. That was in '37 I think he left. He left the band. He didn't want to travel with the band. You know, he was kind of timid. He was a nice kind of fella. 'Nah, I don't want to -- I don't like' --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
you know. He didn't want to go. He told me he wasn't going on the road no more. I think Pete Clark came in and took his place.
Yeah, Louie Jordon. Yeah, Louie was around town trying to get started.
Yeah, getting back to the Louie Jordon part of the band.
